source.title: Enhancing Scalability of Pre-trained Language Models via Efficient Parameter Sharing
source.authors: Peiyu Liu; Ze-Feng Gao; Yu-Shuo Chen; Xin Zhao; Ji-Rong Wen

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream GLUE performance across MPOBERT models of different depths, which bears on downstream performance versus scale, but it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit the original scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. as motivation but does not test power-law loss, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. Its own claim-bearing measurements are downstream GLUE scores for different MPOBERT sizes/depths; these are not pretraining-loss measurements or fitted scaling curves.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. only as motivation. It proposes MPOBERT, a parameter-sharing architecture, and reports its own method's GLUE scores against baselines. It measures no pretraining loss and fits no scaling curve. Its only within-family size comparison is two MPOBERT variants (12 vs 48 layers). These differ in depth, width and parameters (20M vs 75M), and two points cannot show downstream performance improving predictably with scale (V6). The comparison shows only that the authors' larger variant scores higher.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MPOBERT scales BERT depth parameter-efficiently through shared MPO central tensors and a stable initialization. They claim it consistently outperforms competing models in supervised, multi-task and few-shot settings. A further claim is that it beats BERT-large GLUE by 0.1 points with fewer parameters than BERT-base.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes MPO-based sharing of central tensors, layer-specific auxiliary tensors and adapters, and an initialization method based on ALBERT; it does not use the original studies' loss-scaling or compute-allocation fitting procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Within the authors' MPO parameter-sharing architecture, the 48-layer, 75M-parameter variant scores higher on GLUE than the 12-layer, 20M-parameter variant. Test averages are 82.6 vs 80.8; multi-task averages are 84.4 vs 82.0. Pretraining ran for only 10k steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth in a cross-layer parameter-shared BERT improves downstream GLUE scores.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The evidence relevant to downstream performance consists of benchmark comparisons, not a fitted relationship or prediction. The paper reports no uncertainty for the GLUE scores, and its authors note that computational constraints prevented evaluation at depths such as 96 layers or more.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's individual task scores and comparisons among other architectures are not separately extracted; the rows record the paper's aggregate GLUE comparisons relevant to downstream performance versus scale.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss is measured across parameters, tokens or compute.
No fitted curves and no extrapolation.
There is no fixed-parameter shape comparison; the 12-layer and 48-layer variants differ in parameter count.
No other modality or training regime is tested.
No predictive relation between scale or loss and downstream performance; only two model sizes of the study's own method.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2 and V6 'supports' label is not justified. The paper never tests whether downstream performance tracks scale predictably. The rows are comparisons of the study's own method variants plus cited baselines. Confounds: the 12-layer and 48-layer variants differ in hidden size; all models are initialized from ALBERT; pretraining is short (10k steps); no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No predictions from smaller runs or comparison with larger-run held-out loss.
No compute-budget sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is measured.
No fixed-parameter-count comparison of architecture details using pretraining loss.
No other modality or training-regime scaling-law test.
The paper reports downstream GLUE comparisons but does not fit or validate a predictive relationship with scale or pretraining loss.
No sensitivity analysis of scaling-law fits, exponents, or compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: MPOBERT12
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream GLUE performance across model depths and sizes.
rows.note: The table reports this score for MPOBERT-12 and compares it with BERT-12.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method with BERT-12, whose 79.1 score is a cited result (Devlin et al.). The row comes from an inference-cost table, not a scaling measurement, so it bears on no version.

rows.subject: MPOBERT-48
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream GLUE performance across model depths and sizes.
rows.note: The paper reports higher GLUE score for the 48-layer model than for MPOBERT-12.
rows.check: This compares two variants of the study's own method that differ in depth, width and parameter count. Two points cannot show a predictable improvement with scale, so the row bears on no version.

rows.subject: MPOBERT12
rows.operation_detail: Compared multi-task GLUE results for MPOBERT models with different depths.
rows.note: The smaller/depth-12 model has a lower average than the depth-48 model in this reported comparison.
rows.check: This is a two-point comparison within the study's own method under multi-task fine-tuning. The subject is MPOBERT12 with MPOBERT48 as baseline, so the framing is inverted. It is not a scaling-law measurement.

rows.subject: MPOBERT48
rows.operation_detail: Compared multi-task GLUE results for MPOBERT models with different depths.
rows.note: The authors describe this as 1.4 points higher on average than BERT12; the table also shows it exceeds MPOBERT12.
rows.check: This is the same two-point comparison within the study's own method. The authors frame it as deep vs shallow against BERT12 (84.4 vs 83.0), not as a scaling test.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported aggregate GLUE comparisons of MPOBERT12 and MPOBERT48
reader_labels.reason: The larger/deeper MPOBERT model scores higher in the reported GLUE comparisons (r2, r4); these results support a directional improvement in these settings, not a predictive scaling law.
